attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as an authoritative Kea DHCP server on the private eth1 network (192.168.50.0/24) shared with node2 and node3, and configured node2/node3 (Alpine) to obtain their eth1 address via DHCP instead of static assignment, entirely via an Ansible playbook (/root/ansible/site.yml) run from the cluster control node (node4). Node2 leased 192.168.50.101/24 and node3 leased 192.168.50.100/24 from node1's DHCP server (192.168.50.1). All four managed nodes were then restarted one at a time via their native reboot mechanism, with proven boot_id changes and verified post-restart recovery of DHCP service, leases, and Ansible manageability (SSH access persisted via VyOS's own config system).
